note: Hazards, refuges and lights are written by hand from general knowledge of the chart and checked against the baked depth; the traffic lanes are written by pipeline/lanes.py. Positions are metres east and north of the course origin and are approximate. Not for navigation.

areas.name: Potato Patch
areas.say: Four Fathom Bank. Breaks in a swell, worst on the ebb
areas.warn: The Potato Patch: Four Fathom Bank, four fathoms and less. The swell stands up and breaks here, worst on a strong ebb. Boats have been lost on it. Keep to the ship channel or the Bonita Channel inshore

areas.name: South Bar
areas.say: The bar south of the channel. Breaks in a big swell
areas.warn: The South Bar: six fathoms, and the swell shortens over it. In a big westerly swell it breaks right across. Stay in the channel then

areas.name: Duxbury Reef
areas.say: Shale ledges a mile off Duxbury Point, awash
areas.warn: Duxbury Reef: a shale ledge running a mile south-east from the point, awash at low water, and the swell breaks on it. Pass outside the buoy

areas.name: Farallon Islands refuge
areas.say: National Wildlife Refuge. No landing. Keep off
areas.warn: Southeast Farallon is a wildlife refuge: a quarter of a million seabirds nest here, and sea lions and elephant seals haul out on the rocks. Nobody lands. Stand off, slow down and keep the noise down

areas.name: Middle Farallon
areas.say: A single rock. Refuge: keep off

areas.name: North Farallones
areas.warn: The North Farallones: bare pinnacles, part of the refuge. No landing, and nothing to anchor in. Give them a wide berth

areas.name: Precautionary area
areas.say: Six miles round the sea buoy. Ships from three lanes meet here, slow down and take their pilots
areas.warn: Inside the precautionary area: ships turn here to pick up pilots and line up for the channel. Watch all round

areas.name: Northern approach, inbound
areas.warn: In the northern traffic lane, where ships run inbound at 12 to 20 knots. Cross it at right angles and do not loiter

areas.name: Northern approach, outbound
areas.warn: In the northern traffic lane, where ships run outbound at 12 to 20 knots. Cross it at right angles and do not loiter

areas.name: Western approach, inbound
areas.warn: In the western traffic lane, where ships run inbound at 12 to 20 knots. Cross it at right angles and do not loiter

areas.name: Western approach, outbound
areas.warn: In the western traffic lane, where ships run outbound at 12 to 20 knots. Cross it at right angles and do not loiter

areas.name: Southern approach, inbound
areas.warn: In the southern traffic lane, where ships run inbound at 12 to 20 knots. Cross it at right angles and do not loiter

areas.name: Southern approach, outbound
areas.warn: In the southern traffic lane, where ships run outbound at 12 to 20 knots. Cross it at right angles and do not loiter

lights.name: Point Bonita
lights.say: The north side of the entrance. Lit since 1855, reached by a footbridge

lights.name: Mile Rocks
lights.say: Two black rocks off Lands End with the stump of a lighthouse on one. The south side of the entrance

lights.name: Point Reyes
lights.say: The windiest and foggiest headland on the coast. The light is halfway down the cliff, under the fog

lights.name: Farallon Light
lights.say: On the top of Southeast Farallon since 1855

lights.name: SF sea buoy
lights.say: The San Francisco approach buoy, where the lightship lay until 1971. Pilots board here

fog.say: Summer here is fog. A bank of low stratus sits on the cold upwelled water and comes in through the Gate each afternoon as the valley heats. Visibility under it can be a few hundred metres, and the ships in the lanes sound their horns
fog.where: Thickest from Point Reyes to the Farallones and over the bar. Drakes Bay, in the lee of Point Reyes, is often clear when the Gate is shut in. This water wants a real fog bank offshore with visibility down to a quarter of a mile in it, not only the marine layer drawn overhead on the Bay

handover.name: the Golden Gate Bridge
handover.say: This water shares the Bay's origin, so a position here is the same position there. A boat crossing this line eastward would carry on in San Francisco Bay
